date: 2026-09-10
notes: v56 changes what an un-annotated inline var infers from a REAL CONSTANT. Until now it took the constant's own type, and that type moves with the VALUE: var a := 1.0 was a Single (4 bytes, about 7 digits), var b := 0.1 right beside it was an Extended (10 bytes), var c := 1.0/3.0 was a Single under -Munleashed and an Extended under -Mdelphi, and var d := 1/2 was a Double. Four declarations, four types, none of them the one Delphi or an explicit var x: Double := ... gives you. The 4-byte case is the one that bites: var pi := 3.14159265358979 quietly kept seven digits, and the same variable widened to fifteen the moment somebody edited the literal to one a Single cannot hold exactly. Lars hit the other end of it in the Lazarus IDE, where code completion and the compiler disagreed about the type. Now an inferred real constant is a Double -- the third rule of the same family as v54's var i := -1 -> NativeInt and var s := 'x' -> the default string type: inference gives the DEFAULT type of a kind, not the narrowest one today's literal happens to fit. Double and not Extended because Extended is an x87-only 80-bit type and Delphi makes Extended an alias of Double on every 64-bit target we ship. RANGE is never lost: 1.0e400 and 1.0e-4000 keep the wider type they were given, because a Double would silently hold +Inf and 0. Precision digits can be, since that is what asking for a Double means. Variables and non-constant expressions keep their own type exactly as Delphi infers them (var m := someSingle is still a Single); an explicit single(1.0) still wins; currency and comp are untouched; and how real CONSTANTS themselves are typed is NOT changed -- that is stock FPC $MINFPCONSTPREC/$EXCESSPRECISION behaviour, byte-identical to upstream, still available explicitly. Compiler-binary-only refresh on v55; no PPU format, RTL or package change, so UNITS ARE STILL THE v52 SET and auto-update.bat can take the ~3.5 MB bin alone. VERIFIED: tinlinevarrealinfer1 57 checks over 10 structural contexts crossed with the mode axis, baseline 37 fails -> 0 under -Munleashed and 36 -> 0 under both -Mdelphi and -Mdelphiunicode, asserting VALUES as well as sizes and including a closure capture; a must-FAIL companion test keeps for var i := 1.0 rejected cleanly; full 1982-test corpus 1981 SAME 0 DIFF after a baseline-vs-baseline control run that was also 0 DIFF; self-host fixpoint stage2==stage3 byte-identical (e6de1f00eccb9b5ccf028bee7e7342ad); and the neighbouring rules are unmoved, tinlinevarnativeint1 45/45 and tinlinevarstrinfer1 20/20 in both modes. WIN64 RUNTIME VERIFIED on these exact bytes under wine64: the shipped exe runs, compiles in a fresh directory with no mkdir, and scores 52/52 under -Munleashed and 49/49 under -Mdelphi on the real-inference matrix, while the PUBLISHED v55 exe fails that same matrix in the same place -- so the harness can still fail. Those counts are lower than the 57 and 54 the same test reports on Linux because five of its corners are guarded by SizeOf(Extended) > SizeOf(Double), and on Win64 Extended IS Double, 8 bytes, exactly as Delphi has it. Which means the only width this fix moves on Windows is the Single one -- var a := 1.0 -- and that alone is enough to fail v55. wine is NOT Windows: it is an independent reimplementation of the Win64 API running the real shipped PE bytes, so this is execution evidence for the code we generate, never a real-Windows sign-off. Nobody has yet run any VibePascal release on real Windows hardware.
